prompt: Repair journal recovery and append handling without changing the exported API. The on-disk format is a concatenation of frames: 4-byte big-endian payload length, 8-byte big-endian sequence, payload, 4-byte big-endian IEEE CRC32 of the sequence bytes plus payload (not the length). MaxPayload is 1 MiB; empty payloads are valid. Encode rejects sequence zero or oversized payload with ErrInvalid and owns its result. Scan(data) returns decoded records, byte offset immediately after the last valid complete frame, and error. Nonzero sequences must strictly increase (gaps allowed). Copy decoded payloads so neither data nor records alias each other. An incomplete final frame is a benign torn tail: return preceding records/offset and nil error, including when fewer than 4 length bytes remain. Once 4 length bytes exist, a length > MaxPayload is corruption even if the body is missing. Complete checksum failures, zero/decreasing/duplicate sequences are corruption: return preceding records/offset plus *CorruptionError{Offset: frame start, Reason: nonempty}. Never skip corruption or accept frames after it. Empty input returns nil,0,nil. AppendFile(path,payloads) scans the existing file, truncates a benign torn tail, then appends the payloads with consecutive sequences starting at last+1 (or 1 for a new/empty file). An empty batch still repairs a torn tail. Reject ANY oversized batch payload or sequence overflow with ErrInvalid before changing existing bytes; corruption must also leave bytes unchanged and return its CorruptionError. Missing files are created; other OS errors propagate. No concurrent writers or crash-atomic transaction guarantees are required. Add tests across the scanner, encoder and file append path.
